title: Scaling Your Trades Business: Picking Project Management Software
summary: As your trades business grows, you outgrow your systems. Here's what to look for in project management software, from job costing to getting paid, and how to test it before you sign up.
body_markdown:
As your trades business grows, you outgrow your systems; notes on scraps of paper move to your phone, cash in envelopes moves to separate[accounts](https://trusspayments.com/blog-posts/introducing-multi-account) , and job profit outgrows your spreadsheet. Project management software is usually next. Here’s what to look for, and how to test it before you sign up.


## Signs you've outgrown your current system


Some of the telltale signs you've outgrown your envelopes, pieces of paper, and even spreadsheets include:


- **You find out a job lost money after it's done.** Nobody tracked labor and materials against the estimate while the work was happening.
- **Scheduling is a group chat.** Crews and subs double-book, or show up before the material does.
- **Invoicing waits until last minute.** Bills go out late, so cash comes in late, putting pressure on margins.
- **Only you know where everything stands.** If you're on a site, nobody in the office can answer a client's question.


If two or more of those sound familiar, you know it's time.


## What to look for in project management software


### 1. Built for jobs, end-to-end


Generic tools are great at to-do lists, but trades businesses need more: jobs with phases, budgets, crews, subs, materials and a client attached. Look for software that understands estimates, change orders and job costing out of the box, so you're not rebuilding a construction workflow inside a tool made for something else.


### 2. Estimates and job costing that stay connected


Good software turns approved estimates into the job budgets, then tracks actual labor and materials against it, live, as the work happens. That's how you catch a job going over while you can still fix it, not after.


### 3. Scheduling for crews and subs


You want one calendar for every crew and sub, with automatic notifications when something changes. Bonus points for the ability to see who's where on a given day.


### 4. A mobile app your field team will actually use


Most of your work happens on site, so the app matters as much as the computer. Check that your crew can clock in, upload photos (or connect a photo app like[CompanyCam](https://companycam.com/) ), and fill out daily logs. If your crew won't use it, your office is working without the full picture.


### 5. Client communication and approvals


A client portal where homeowners can see progress, approve estimates and e-sign change orders saves you dozens of calls a month. It also gives you a trail if there's a dispute about what was agreed.


### 6. Invoicing and payments built in


This is where a lot of software falls short, and it's the part that pays your bills. Look for:


- **Progress and milestone invoicing** , not just one invoice at the end
- **Online payments** by bank transfer and card
- **Automatic reminders** on unpaid invoices
- **How fast money lands.** Ask how many days a payment takes to reach your account, and what it costs.
- **Paying out, not just getting paid.** You also pay subs and suppliers so check whether the system handles that, or connects to something that does.


### 7. Reporting you can act on


You don't need 40 charts. You need a handful of answers: which jobs are profitable, which are over budget, what's been invoiced but not paid, and what the next few weeks look like for your crew.


### 8. Room to grow


Check how pricing changes as you add users, crews or locations, and whether the features you'll grow into are available, or locked behind a much bigger plan.


### 9. Real support


When you need support, how fast can you reach a human? Look at support hours, channels (phone, chat, email), what onboarding help is included, and whether you get a dedicated account manager.


## How to choose: a simple process


1. **Write down your top three problems.** Late invoices? Slim margins? Scheduling chaos? Those are your must-haves.
2. **Shortlist two or three options built for the trades.** Skip tools you'd have to bend to fit your trade.
3. **Run a real job through the trial.** Don't just click around a demo. Take one current job from estimate to invoice and see where it gets stuck.
4. **Put your PM in the trial.** If your best crew lead hates the app, adoption will stall.
5. **Check every integration you need.** Accounting and payments first.
6. **Count the full cost.** Subscription, payment processing fees, setup, training and the hours you'll save.


## Who to choose


The right tool depends on the size of your jobs and how you run them.
